evidence.text: The Eel slides over a ledger. “Three customers, one allowance. Please check my addition before I become a very embarrassed night-light.” Compare the supplied endpoint demands with the delivered budget. You can practice, ask for help, retry or leave. No timer, tool or recruited ally is required.

The fictional allowance is 30 W delivered to the endpoints after losses. The audit cards request 12 W, 11 W and 10 W at that same delivered boundary. Each occupied port and every other compatibility requirement is already checked for this exercise. The aggregate total still needs checking. A power or link lamp cannot enlarge the budget; adequate power alone does not prove data connectivity.

You identified the ledger’s shortfall: 12 W + 11 W + 10 W = 33 W, exceeding the fictional delivered 30 W budget by 3 W. The Eel recorded the diagnosis and dedicated a ledger decoration to the Workshop. The proposal remains over budget; the audit changes no equipment and proves no data link.

alternatives.label: Submit the energy audit
alternatives.explanation: Identify whether the full ledger fits its delivered allowance, and state the headroom or excess in watts. Correctly identifying the 3 W excess completes this optional diagnosis once. Practice does not award the workshop decoration.

sourceClaims.section: Introductory PSE/PD definitions; PoE budget; PoE class, table headings for power delivered to PD versus switch-port output
sourceClaims.supportedClaim: PSE output and power delivered to a PD are distinct accounting boundaries. Multiple devices must fit the available aggregate budget.
limitations: Only this distinction and aggregate-budget concept are used. No table wattages, PoE class allocation, priority behavior or detection timing are used by the fiction.

model.label: fictional-teaching-profile
model.scope: An optional diagnosis of the reviewed 30 W delivered-power ledger. Reuse C-POWER, T10 and B-POWER-30 without changing their demands, units, inclusive ceiling or accounting boundary.
assumptions: Budget and every endpoint demand are supplied at the delivered endpoint boundary after losses.
Each occupied port and all other compatibility checks are independently satisfied in these three reviewed examples.
The activity is available at the Shell Market without recruitment, inventory, another optional activity, a main-objective completion or a score.
limitations: The 30 W value is a fictional teaching allowance, not a universal PoE standard or product rating.
No PoE class, voltage negotiation, inrush model, per-port wattage threshold or extra PSE-to-PD loss subtraction is modeled.
An acceptable aggregate total cannot override an independently failed port or compatibility check.
Correctly diagnosing the 33 W plan leaves it over budget; the diagnosis does not repair equipment or complete O09.
Adequate power alone does not prove a data link or end-to-end service. No fiber electrical-power delivery is modeled.

method.text: Keep the same accounting boundary: every figure is delivered watts after losses. Add the demand cards, compare the sum with 30 W, then report the spare watts or shortfall.

workedStep.text: The first two cards total 12 W + 11 W = 23 W. That leaves 7 W of the 30 W allowance. The last audit card asks for 10 W. Compare that demand with the remaining 7 W.

solution.text: 12 W + 11 W + 10 W = 33 W. Choose “Over budget” and enter 3 W excess. This correctly diagnoses an over-budget plan; it does not repair it. Using this answer records assisted completion and earns the same decoration.

observableOutcome: A correct full audit records one diagnosis and one cosmetic workshop reward. The ledger remains over budget. Wrong answers receive an explanation and retry; practice awards nothing. Exit closes the ledger at the captured Shell Market location with required inventory and main progress intact.
completionExplanation: “Three watts too ambitious,” says the Eel, stamping the ledger. “Your addition has saved my reputation.” You identified 33 W of demand against 30 W delivered: a 3 W shortfall. Your workshop ledger decoration is earned. The audit records a diagnosis; the proposal remains over budget and data connectivity is unproven.

instructions: The Eel has three demand cards and one allowance. “Would you audit these before I sign something luminous?”
For the full audit, add 12 W, 11 W and 10 W. The fictional allowance is 30 W delivered after losses. Choose within budget or over budget, then enter the headroom or excess in watts.
Every occupied port and other compatibility check is already satisfied for this exercise. Practice, hints, retry and exit are always available. Take your time.

practice.explanation: 12 W + 11 W = 23 W. The 30 W delivered allowance leaves 7 W headroom. Practice changes no equipment and does not complete the full audit.

boundaryExample.explanation: 12 W + 11 W + 7 W = 30 W. Equality fits the fictional inclusive allowance, with 0 W headroom. Independent port and compatibility checks still matter; adequate power does not prove data connectivity.

answerControls.assessmentLabel: Does this ledger fit its delivered allowance?

practice.correct: Yes: 23 W fits the delivered 30 W allowance with 7 W headroom. The full audit is still waiting.
practice.incorrect: The practice cards total 23 W, leaving 7 W headroom. Choose “Within budget” and enter 7 W. No audit or reward has been recorded.
practice.invalidInput: Choose within budget or over budget and enter a nonnegative number of watts for this practice answer. No answer has been judged.

Your workshop ledger decoration is earned. The audit records a diagnosis; the proposal remains over budget and data connectivity is unproven.
delivery.incorrect: The full ledger asks for 33 W against a delivered 30 W allowance: 3 W too much. A lamp does not add watts. Choose “Over budget” and enter 3 W. You can retry or leave; no audit reward has been recorded.

feedback.contentError: The ledger’s supplied figures cannot be checked. This is a problem with the exhibit, not your answer. No penalty or reward was recorded. You can leave safely.
feedback.alreadyCompleted: Your audit and workshop ledger decoration are already recorded. Read the explanation or practice again whenever you like.

recovery.retryExplanation: Begin a new ledger attempt. Keep clues, personal notes and hint history; previous-attempt measurements remain visibly stale. Retry does not consume a tool, alter main progress or save the adventure.
recovery.exitExplanation: Close the ledger at the same Shell Market place where you opened it. Keep required inventory, main progress and party. Leaving does not move you, refresh a measurement or save the adventure.

reward.alternativeText: A framed delivered-power ledger: one 30 W allowance tray faces three demand tiles labeled 12 W, 11 W and 10 W; their 33 W total is marked 3 W over budget.
reward.unavailableText: Your workshop ledger decoration is recorded. Its picture cannot be displayed here; the description and audit remain readable.
